html:
Robert Clive was the East India Company officer who won Bengal for the Company. He began British rule in India and made himself one of the richest men in Britain.

He was sent to Madras as a clerk at eighteen, was bored and unhappy, and turned soldier in the Carnatic Wars. His defence of Arcot in 1751 made him famous.

In 1756 the nawab of Bengal took Calcutta. Clive retook it, plotted with the nawab's commander and bankers, and won the Battle of Plassey in 1757. The new nawab paid him about £234,000 and later a land grant worth £27,000 a year.

He came back as governor in 1765 and took for the Company the right to collect the taxes of Bengal. He tried to stop the private trade and gift-taking by which Company men, himself included, had grown rich.

The Bengal famine of 1770 and the Company's near-bankruptcy turned opinion against him. Questioned by Parliament in 1772 about his gains, he said that when he thought of the gold he could have taken, he was astonished at his own moderation. He was cleared. He was often ill and took opium, and he died by his own hand in 1774, aged forty-nine.
sum: Robert Clive was the East India Company officer who won Bengal for the Company. He began British rule in India and made himself one of the richest men in Britain.
